excerpts.text: ## Q. Performance Budget
### Benchmark fixture
| Dimension | P12A proof | Full target | Stress gate |
| active AI rivals | 3 | 6–10 | 12 |
| concurrent rival projects | 3–6 | 12–30 | 48 |
| weeks | 6,240 no-churn (plus 520-week smoke/save checkpoints) | 6,240 | 6,240 |
| historical rival films | fixture-derived | 2,000–3,500 expected envelope | at least 4,000 synthetic/organic |
| closed/inactive studios | 0 | retained | 50 archived identities fixture |
### Time budgets
- isolated rival subsystem at stress gate: ≤3 s over 6,240 weeks on the recorded CI/reference machine;
- incremental weekly rival step: median ≤0.5 ms, p95 ≤2 ms;
- no weekly operation scans all historical films, events, contracts, or transactions;
- quarterly ranking/pulse aggregation: ≤10 ms at stress fixture;
- rival profile first page projection: ≤10 ms from indexed state.

Full-save operations must be timed independently at the P12A/full/stress fixtures: canonical serialize, digest, strict validate/import, load-to-ready, and durable write. Provisional interaction gates are canonical serialize+digest p95 ≤100 ms at full target (≤200 ms stress), validate/import p95 ≤500 ms (≤1 s stress), and asynchronous persistence end-to-end p95 ≤250 ms at full target. Any synchronous main-thread storage step exceeding 50 ms is a ship blocker; change the storage/caching architecture rather than loosening history retention.
Record hardware, runtime version, commit, fixture seed, counts, warm-up, repetitions, median/p95/max, and allocation/heap evidence. A faster machine is not a complexity fix.
| Canonical full-save serialize + digest | p95 ≤ 100 ms full-target / ≤ 200 ms stress |
| Strict validate/import | p95 ≤ 500 ms full-target / ≤ 1 s stress |
| Asynchronous durable write, end-to-end | p95 ≤ 250 ms full-target; no synchronous main-thread step > 50 ms |

**CURRENT CODE VERIFIED — The existing V14 save-size harness provides a useful floor, not a rival projection.** `scripts/measure-v14-save-size.mts` records 715,193 bytes at week 520 for a continuously operating player studio with 114 releases. Its 26-week event policy leaves 30,473 event bytes versus 202,925 bytes in the unwindowed comparison, while durable wrap/premiere history remains. Package 12 should copy that tiering discipline, not extrapolate the exact bytes as a multi-studio budget.

Current code already has multiple full-save amplification paths. Every tick calls `assertStudioPlacementInvariants()`; while evaluating historical facility-opex rows, `expectedWeeklyOperatingCostAt()` rebuilds `demolishedFacilityHistory()` from the whole ledger. The browser `stableStringify`s and rewrites the full save after every authoritative transition. Combined with projected localStorage quota pressure, this makes both CPU and persistence—not merely rival-loop time—horizon blockers. P12 must not “solve” them by pruning authoritative player history: optimize maintained indexes/aggregates, measure serialize/validate/load/write separately, and adopt an appropriate asynchronous storage path before the 120-year ship gate.

finding.originalRequirement: Asynchronous durable write/persistence end-to-end p95<=250ms at the full target. Canonical serialize/digest and strict validate/import have separately named limits; load-to-ready and durable write must be timed independently.
finding.notExplicitlyRequired: The sources do not define250ms as a cap on the entire campaign operation from coordinator.campaign, including proposal/fork/checkpoint strict/history/codec preparation, to returned accepted response.
finding.correction: Withdraw the categorical complete campaign Save MISS250ms assignment in my final-measurement-disposition.{json,md} and prior measurement-disposition.json. It was a phase interpretation mistakenly stated as the original requirement. Preserve the actual measured complete Save latency as a separate reference cost.
finding.persistenceBoundaryInterpretation: DES§34 names durable write end-to-end and PERF008/009 independently name write, so this is more specific than treating every prerequisite CPU operation and campaign transaction as the250ms phase. The pin does not explicitly map later worker-message/queue/codec boundaries into this phase; those implementation scopes must remain documented.
